threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know they’re new when they don’t yet know the best spots for a late-night kebab after a gig—everyone's got a favorite, it’s a rite of passage.
Caught a guy in a tweed coat ordering a kebab while pretending to conduct an orchestra. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when the bakery on Sonnenallee started saving me a piece of my favorite cake every Friday. It felt like family.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a 24/7 Döner that’s packed at 3 AM with locals debating the best street art. It's a rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a true local when they can name the exact time the BART delays kick in during rush hour, and it’s not just the usual 5 o’clock traffic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a guy playing sax on the 49 going over the bridge, traffic stopped. He turned it into a serenade for the passengers—crowd loved it.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all love the Festa Major de Gràcia, but many locals just want to avoid the crowds and get back to our usual life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the Pl. del Sol roundabout, staring confusedly at the bike lanes while holding a map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'tube' instead of 'the Overground' when catching a train from Dalston Junction. Classic newbie mistake.
Last night on the 36, a guy serenaded an invisible crowd. He claimed the moon was his biggest fan. Only in Peckham, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids turning an empty lot into a soccer field with just some worn-out shoes for goals. That’s Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You hear a random punk concert in the park every Sunday in Kreuzberg, an unplanned jam session that seems to unite everyone. Never seen that elsewhere.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can navigate the BART delays while still hustling a burrito from El Farolito, without missing a beat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy serenading the 49 bus riders with an accordion at Larkin. The crowd’s mix of smiles and confusion—classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the 'Gràcia vibe' is just for Instagram pics, but locals know it's really about stealing moments in the quiet plazas, not the crowded streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell the newbies by their wide-eyed look at the ferias de barrio—amazed by the decades-old traditions they stumble upon.
